They use the sudden schedule changes and the weird seating choices, and whenever I try to point it out to someone else in the group, the people doing it just pull out those same emails or notes that supposedly explain it all away. So everyone else just looks at the notes and believes them. \n\nSpeaking of notes, actually, we switched to using iPads for our sheet music this season. It's supposed to save paper, which is great, but the glare from the stage lights is just terrible. We played at this historic theater downtown last weekend—beautiful acoustics, built in like 1924, I think—and the lighting guy absolutely refused to dim the overheads. I had to order one of those matte screen protectors online, but I could not get the air bubbles out of the corners. Have you ever tried putting one of those on a large tablet? It is literally impossible to keep the dust out. The tubes are like two feet long. And they hung it right outside my bedroom window. Every time the wind picks up, it sounds like a cathedral bell going off. I mean, I appreciate good resonance as much as the next guy, but at 3:00 AM, it's a bit much. \n\nI actually tried to buy them a smaller, wooden one as a sort of passive-aggressive gift, but the hardware store down the street was closed for renovation. They’re putting in this new coffee shop attached to it, which is weird, right? Coffee and power tools. Seems like a liability waiting to happen. I used an angle grinder once for a sound art installation I was working on in grad school, and even with the safety goggles, I was terrified. The sparks flew everywhere, and I ended up singing the sleeve of my favorite sweater. It was this really nice merino wool one my sister got me in Ireland. \n\nBut, uh... no, to answer your question, I don't hear any voices. Just the wind chimes. The bags have these really intricate illustrations on them, though—like, line drawings of toucans and jaguars. \n\nMy cousin used to draw like that. I got it at this little boutique downtown that sells all these imported soaps and artisanal honey. The honey was good, though. He had this massive collection of Isaac Asimov and Arthur C. Clarke. The covers always had those amazing, retro-futuristic paintings on them, you know? The ones with the giant geometric spaceships and the weirdly colored planets. I actually tried to find some of those specific editions online a while back, just for nostalgia.
